summary.text: Guy Reschenthaler is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 14th District, serving since January 2019. A former Navy Judge Advocate General (JAG) Corps attorney who deployed to Iraq, he later served as a magisterial district judge and a Pennsylvania state senator before winning his House seat. In the 119th Congress he is House Republican Chief Deputy Whip and a member of the Appropriations Committee.

paragraphs.text: Reschenthaler was born in Pittsburgh in 1983, and his House website says he is the son of former teachers and was raised in southwestern Pennsylvania.
He graduated from Penn State, The Behrend College (B.A., 2004, per Wikipedia) and from Duquesne University School of Law (J.D., 2007, per Wikipedia).
After law school he joined the U.S. Navy Judge Advocate General's Corps and volunteered for duty in Iraq.

According to his House website, he prosecuted nearly 100 terrorists in Baghdad, defended a Navy SEAL in a case related to the capture of the "Butcher of Fallujah," and later served as Officer in Charge of the Naval Legal Service Office for Texas and Oklahoma.
He then returned to southwestern Pennsylvania, where he practiced law and, per his House website, was a partner in a real estate brokerage and related businesses employing roughly a dozen people.
Reschenthaler was elected Magisterial District Judge in 2013, winning the nomination of both parties, and served in that role from 2013 to 2015.
In 2015 he was elected to the Pennsylvania State Senate to represent the 37th District (parts of Allegheny and Washington counties), and he served until 2019.
He was elected to the U.S. House in 2018 and sworn in for a fourth term on January 3, 2025.
He became House Republican Chief Deputy Whip in January 2023 and, in the 118th Congress (2023–2024), also sat on Appropriations, per Ballotpedia.
His House website says he serves on the Appropriations Committee, including its Energy and Water Development, Interior and Environment, and National Security, Department of State subcommittees.
